To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
African-American caregivers perceive that mental health care services for their adolescents are not as important as other health issues and are not accessible to them due to financial reasons.
African-American caregivers’ perceptions of mental health care barriers are influenced by their experiences, social support, early recognition by school systems and extrinsic behavior.

African-American caregivers of adolescents with a mental health disorder are influenced in their mental healthcare-seeking behavior by their perceptions of mental health, previous experiences with mental health care, and the ability of mental health professionals to engage their adolescents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of barriers to mental healthcare access and the impact of these barriers on African-American caregiver mental healthcare-seeking behavior.
the identification of factors that affect African-American caregiver health-seeking behavior for their adolescents with mental health problems.
how African-American caregivers perceive and experience barriers to mental health services for adolescents with mental disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
African-American caregiver perceptions regarding socio-ecological factors influence their decision-making when seeking care for their adolescents with mental health problems.

African-American caregiver experiences with mental health issues, social support, and previous experiences with mental health care influence their mental health-seeking behaviors for their adolescent children.
African-American caregivers of adolescents with a mental health disorder experience multiple barriers to mental health services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the socio-ecological model of health behavior is useful in understanding the barriers and health-seeking behaviors of African-American caregivers of adolescents with a mental health diagnosis.
African-American caregivers who have experienced mental health issues themselves are better equipped to recognize mental health issues in adolescents.
caregivers who experienced positive mental health experiences were more likely to utilize mental healthcare resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mental health is a priority and that caregivers are more likely to seek care if they have had positive previous experiences with mental health services.
healthcare providers should be aware of the importance of the family unit when engaging adolescents and caregivers in mental healthcare services.
mental health care providers need to be aware of the socio-ecological factors that affect African-American caregivers’ mental health care-seeking behavior.
